subject: Tiered commit scenarios for Hosted API — pricing proposal and next steps
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Omar Shah <omar@quantumhealth.com>, Ellen Park <ellen.park@quantumhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-08T09:12:00-04:00
Subject: Proposal: tiered commit scenarios for Hosted API (Quantum Health)

Hi Omar / Ellen,

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday — below is a concise set of tiered commit scenarios for Hosted API usage that reflect the breakpoints we discussed. I attached a spreadsheet with the math so you can toggle volumes. High-level: we can structure the deal as committed monthly tokens (billed monthly against a committed amount) with per-token overage, and two optional discount mechanics: marginal discounts (discount applies only to tokens above a breakpoint) or blended discounts (single effective rate across total committed volume).

Proposed scenarios (monthly committed tokens):
- Scenario A (Conservative): 100M / 500M / 2B breakpoints — discounts: 0% / 10% / 22% (marginal)
- Scenario B (Growth): 250M / 1B / 5B breakpoints — discounts: 5% / 18% / 30% (marginal)
- Scenario C (Blended offer): effective blended rates for 1B commitment = $0.00045/token (vs list $0.00060) with a 12-month minimum

Key questions for Quantum Health:
1) Do you prefer marginal (clear per-breakpoint discounts) or blended (simpler billing but different renewal mechanics)?
2) Are you able to commit to a 12- or 24-month minimum? We can offer deeper discounts for longer terms.
3) Any procurement constraints (PO, DocuSign cadence, required CLINs) we should plan for?

Next steps: If you confirm which scenario you prefer I’ll loop in Legal/Finance for finalized terms and send a DocuSign. I attached the spreadsheet for the exact token math.

Thanks,
Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sergio@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachment: QH-pricing-scenarios.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Omar Shah <omar@quantumhealth.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Cc: Ellen Park <ellen.park@quantumhealth.com>
Date: 2026-07-09T11:03:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: tiered commit scenarios for Hosted API (Quantum Health)

Sergio —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the spreadsheet. A few clarifying questions before we escalate to procurement: 
- For Scenario B (250M / 1B / 5B) can you show the effective blended rate for a 12-month ARR if we land on the middle tier (1B/mo)? Our CFO likes a single-line blended figure rather than marginal math.
- If we exceed committed tokens in a given month, what’s the overage charge? Is it the next marginal tier rate or a fixed overage premium?
- We prefer a 12-month minimum but need to confirm with Procurement if they can sign within two weeks.

Also: our security team asked whether audit logs and token-level usage reports can be provided monthly for cost reconciliation. Is that standard?

If you can reply with a simple example (e.g., 1B committed, actual usage 1.3B — show billed amount for marginal vs blended), that would help.

Thanks,
Omar Shah
Head of Product, Quantum Health
omar@quantumhealth.com

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Omar Shah <omar@quantumhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-09T13:08:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: tiered commit scenarios for Hosted API (Quantum Health)

Omar —

Great questions. Quick answers inline and a short example below; full math is in the attached spreadsheet. Also, yes — audit logs and per-token usage exports are standard for Dedicated/Hosted customers; we can provide monthly CSV exports and a dashboard snapshot.

- Blended vs Marginal example (Scenario B):
  * List price: $0.00060/token (baseline)
  * Marginal tiers: 250M @0% -> next 750M @18% discount -> 4B @30% discount
  * If committed = 1B and actual = 1.3B: marginal billing charges tokens at each tier rate (first 250M at list, next 750M at tier rate, additional 300M at 30% discount rate). Effective blended rate in that month = total billed / total tokens.
  * Blended option: single effective rate applied to total usage (easier for finance — straightforward invoice line).

- Overage: we typically bill overage at the marginal tier rate (not a punitive premium) unless you prefer an overage cap or a prepaid buffer. We can also implement a rollover credit policy for monthly variance.

- Procurement: we can target a 2-week turnaround for 12-month SOW + DocuSign; Finance will need the HubSpot deal id (see below).

I attached an example calc: 1B committed, actual 1.3B — marginal billed: $XXX, blended billed: $YYY (see spreadsheet). Let me know which format CFO prefers and I’ll push the final quote.

Best,
Sergio

Attachment: QH-pricing-scenarios.xlsx

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-10T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Quantum Health — quick pricing approval ask

Team —

Looping you both in on the Quantum Health conversation. They like Scenario B but CFO wants a blended headline. Quantum asked if we can compress the second breakpoint to 600M (so tiers become 250M / 600M / 4.15B) to make their forecasting simpler. They are asking for a commercial exception: move the 18% discount threshold down to 600M instead of 1B.

My ask: can we approve a one-time experimental breakpoint shift for this customer (12-month committed minimum) that results in an effective blended mid-tier of ~ $0.00048/token at 1B committed? If yes, we can close faster. If not, I’ll push the marginal explanation again.

Reasons to approve: accelerates close, higher probability of cross-sell into Dedicated in year 2.
Risks: slightly compresses price ladder — minimal impact if we preserve 24-month cap on renewal discounts.

Tagged: Marissa for legal/terms risk, Karthik for pricing approval.

Thanks,
Sergio

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-10T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Quantum Health — quick pricing approval ask

Sergio —

Thanks for the context. I ran the numbers against our unit economics and the proposed experimental breakpoint (250M / 600M / 4.15B) is acceptable for a 12-month committed deal with these guardrails:
- Require a signed 12-month SOW with a minimum monthly commit of 1B tokens aggregated across product usage.
- Offer the compressed breakpoint as a promotional one-time concession; include a clause that future renewal discounts will reset to standard ladder unless we agree otherwise during renewal negotiation.
- No marketing or case-study requirements baked in (leave that as optional).

I can approve a blended headline at ~$0.00048/token for the 1B commit scenario and the overage rules remain marginal (overage billed at tier rates). Please push the updated quote into HubSpot (deal QH-2026-027) and attach the DocuSign link. I’ll notify Finance to expect the SOW.

Karthik
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Omar Shah <omar@quantumhealth.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@quantumhealth.com>, Ellen Park <ellen.park@quantumhealth.com>
Date: 2026-07-12T16:40:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: tiered commit scenarios for Hosted API (Quantum Health)

Sergio / Karthik —

Thanks — that all sounds good. We prefer the blended headline for CFO simplicity, and the 12-month SOW with the compressed breakpoint is acceptable. Please send the final DocuSign for signature (procurement@quantumhealth.com). Also confirm that we will receive monthly token-usage CSVs and a billing dashboard snapshot for reconciliation.

Once Procurements signs we’ll onboard next week.

Best,
Omar

Attachment: redwood-commit-terms-docusign.pdf (placeholder, DocuSign link provided)
